title: Myth vs fact: radiation from medical scans

slides.title: Worried about radiation from a scan?
3 myths, busted.
steps: Fact: MRI uses a magnet and radio waves. Ultrasound uses sound waves. No radiation.
Fact: a chest X-ray is about the same as 10 days of the natural radiation all around us.
Fact: please ask. Your doctor weighs the benefit of every scan against its small risk.

captions.gbp:
Worried about radiation from a medical scan? Here are the facts. MRI uses a magnet and radio waves, and ultrasound uses sound waves, so neither uses any radiation. Scans that do use radiation use very small amounts: a chest X-ray is about the same as 10 days of the natural background radiation we all receive, a DEXA bone density scan about 3 hours, and a screening mammogram about 34 days. Before any X-ray, CT or mammogram, tell us and your doctor if you are or might be pregnant, keep a simple list of the scans you've had, and send past images to new doctors to avoid repeats. It's always OK to ask whether a scan without radiation could answer the question. Our team in Seminole is happy to answer your questions before you book.

Book online at advancedimg.com. General information, not medical advice. Sources: CDC; RadiologyInfo.org (ACR, RSNA).

carousel: A smiling technologist beside a patient lying on an open MRI table. Myth vs fact: worried about radiation from a scan? Let's clear it up.

3 myths, busted. Every scan uses radiation: false, MRI and ultrasound use none. X-ray doses are big: a chest X-ray is about 10 days of natural radiation. It's rude to ask: please ask, your doctor weighs benefit against a small risk.
About the same as everyday natural radiation for: 0 for MRI or ultrasound, 3 hours for a DEXA scan, 10 days for a chest X-ray, 34 days for a screening mammogram.
Before any X-ray, CT or mammogram: tell us first if you are or could be pregnant; keep a list of your scans; share past images so you can skip repeats; ask if a scan without radiation could work.
Questions about a scan? Just ask us. Call (727) 398-5999 or use the link in bio.

facts_checked: MRI/ultrasound no ionizing radiation, patient tips: CDC Facts About Imaging Procedures (reviewed 2026-07-15). Doses vs background (chest X-ray 0.1 mSv/10 days, DEXA 0.001 mSv/3 h, screening digital mammo 0.28 mSv/34 days, ~3 mSv/yr): RadiologyInfo.org X-ray page (ACR/RSNA, reviewed 2025-04-15). Checked 2026-10-13.
flag: Website DEXA FAQ (services-data.ts ~line 1546) says DEXA is 'about 1/10th the dose of a standard chest X-ray'; RadiologyInfo gives 0.001 vs 0.1 mSv (about 1/100). X-ray FAQ (~line 1449) says 'a few days' of background; RadiologyInfo says about 10 days.
